title: それでも — “even so / still”
summary: A conjunction placed at the start of a sentence: despite the previous situation, the opposite result or action still happens.

patterns.gloss: 文 + それでも + 文 (雨でした。それでも試合をした。)

body.p: それ = the situation just described, でも = even with that. Despite that situation, what follows is unchanged.
でも simply links contrasting content. それでも adds strength to a will or fact: “even so, still …”. それなのに carries more complaint.

examples.ja: 雨（あめ）でした。それでも試合（しあい）は行（おこな）われました。
examples.romaji: Ame deshita. Sore demo shiai wa okonawaremashita.
examples.tr: It was raining. Even so, the game was held.

examples.ja: 何度（なんど）も失敗（しっぱい）した。それでも彼（かれ）は諦（あきら）めなかった。
examples.romaji: Nando mo shippai shita. Sore demo kare wa akiramenakatta.
examples.tr: He failed many times. Even so, he didn't give up.

examples.ja: みんなに反対（はんたい）された。それでも私（わたし）はやってみたい。
examples.romaji: Minna ni hantai sareta. Sore demo watashi wa yatte mitai.
examples.tr: Everyone was against it. Even so, I want to try.

pitfalls: Use it at the start of a sentence, after a full stop.
For strong complaint, それなのに fits better.
